transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi doc. I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. Like my engine's always running and I can’t just idle, you know? 

Speaking of engines, I was actually just down at my brother-in-law's garage this past weekend. He's rebuilding this '72 Chevelle. Beautiful car, really. We spent like three hours trying to track down a vacuum leak. It's funny how they used to build those things, you know? So much room under the hood compared to my Honda. I took the Honda in for a simple oil change last week and the guy tried to upsell me on a cabin air filter for like eighty bucks! I told him I could buy the part at AutoZone for fifteen and do it myself in five minutes. I mean, the nerve of some of these places, right? 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, my job. Yeah, I do customer service, and they recently changed everything around on us. And this new work setup has just made it a lot harder to hide the fact that I can't stay put. It's all open now, no tall cubicle walls, so everybody can see every time I get up or shift around.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

No, not really. I mean, I've always been a pretty energetic guy, you know? But not like... unusually energetic or anything. I usually get my six or seven hours of sleep. Sometimes less if the dog wakes me up. We have this golden retriever, Buster, and he's got this habit of needing to go out right at 3:00 AM. Every single night. It’s like he’s got a little alarm clock in his head. My wife says I should just ignore him, but if I do, he starts doing this low whine that drives me absolutely crazy. 

And speaking of sleep, I tried one of those memory foam pillows recently because my neck was bothering me. Supposed to be the best thing ever, right? Cost me forty bucks at Target. Honestly, it feels like sleeping on a brick. I don't get the hype. I ended up giving it to Buster, and he loves it. Go figure. But yeah, no weird racing thoughts or needing less sleep, just the usual stuff.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks, especially ones that aren’t very interesting to you?

Yeah, definitely. Especially at work. Like, we have these longer coaching meetings now, or they'll hand out a new procedure to read through. I always start off fine, you know? I'm looking right at it. But after a few minutes, I realize my eyes are just moving across the page and I haven't taken in a single word of what I just read or what they just said. 

It’s like when I try to read the manual for the new smoker I bought. It’s an offset smoker, one of those heavy steel ones. I’ve been trying to perfect my brisket for, gosh, three years now. The secret is really in the wood you use. Hickory is classic, but I’ve been experimenting with pecan wood lately. It gives it this sweeter smoke that just pairs perfectly with a good dry rub. My neighbor, Dave, he swears by applewood, but I think it’s too mild for beef. He’s always trying to tell me how to barbecue, which is rich coming from a guy who burns hot dogs on a gas grill. Gas grills, I mean, what's the point? You might as well just cook it in the oven. 

But yeah, if it's something boring like those work procedures, my brain just kind of checks out after a couple of minutes.
Do you often feel worried or anxious, especially in situations where most people wouldn’t be?

Anxious? No, not really. I don't sit around worrying about things out of the blue. My wife, though, she worries enough for the both of us. Like last week, she was absolutely convinced the water heater was going to burst because it was making this low humming noise. I told her, it's just a fifteen-year-old unit with some sediment build-up. You gotta flush those things out once a year. Most people don't know that. You just hook a regular garden hose up to the valve at the bottom and let it drain out into the driveway. The amount of white calcium and junk that comes out is just unbelievable. 

Hard water will absolutely destroy your appliances if you aren't careful. We had a dishwasher give out after just five years because the heating element got completely caked in scale. I ended up pulling the whole unit out myself, which was a total nightmare because whoever put the tile floor in the kitchen laid it right in front of the dishwasher, so it was basically trapped in there. I had to pry the little leveling feet up with a crowbar just to clear the lip of the tile. Scratched up the cabinet a bit, but you can't really tell unless you're looking for it. 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I'm pretty laid back about most things. I don't really get anxious like that.
Do you often act on impulse or find yourself jumping into activities without thinking them through first?

Impulsive? Hmm, I don't know if I'd say impulsive. I mean, I don't just jump out of airplanes or anything crazy like that. I guess I do sometimes just decide to do something and go for it, but it's usually not a big deal. Like last weekend, I was just sitting there watching the game—college football, you know, because the NFL has just gotten way too commercialized. Every two minutes it's a car commercial or some insurance ad with an emu. It really ruins the flow of the game. 

Anyway, I was watching the game, and I suddenly decided I needed to reorganize the garage. Right then and there. Missed the entire fourth quarter. But the garage had been bothering me for months. You see, I have this pegboard system for my tools. It’s a great system if you actually put things back where they belong. But I had my socket wrenches mixed up with the screwdrivers, and don't even get me started on the metric versus standard situation. It was a disaster. I ended up buying these little plastic bins that hook right into the pegboard. Found them at the hardware store down the street—the local one, not the big box store. I try to support local businesses when I can, even if their prices are a little higher. The guy who runs it, Frank, he's been there since the eighties. Knows everything about everything. You go in there looking for a specific bolt, and he just walks right to the back and pulls it out of a dusty drawer. It's amazing. 

So yeah, I guess I just decided to do the garage right then, but I wouldn't call it acting without thinking. The garage needed doing, you know?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you can't sit still for very long?

Restless? Well, I don't feel like I have to get up and run a marathon or anything, but I guess I'm always moving a little bit. Like at work, even when I’m trying to look completely calm while I'm dealing with a customer complaint, my foot is just going a mile a minute bouncing under the desk. Or I’m clicking a pen. I do that a lot in those coaching meetings I mentioned earlier, just clicking away without really noticing it until someone gives me a look. 

I always use those Pilot G2 pens, the 0.7 millimeter ones in blue. The 0.5 fine point ones scratch the paper way too much, but the 0.7 is just a really smooth line. And they have this really satisfying click to them. The problem is, everyone else at the call center knows they're the best pens, so if you leave one out on your desk, it’s gone by lunch. I actually started buying them in bulk myself and keeping them locked in my top drawer. You wouldn't believe how petty grown adults get over office supplies. Just last month, Brenda from accounting sent out this passive-aggressive, company-wide email about a missing stapler. A standard, heavy-duty black stapler. Like anyone really wanted to steal it. They push us to be a paperless office now anyway. We handle almost all the customer service tickets through the online portal, so I don't even know what she's stapling over there. Probably just printing out emails to file them in a cabinet, which completely defeats the purpose of the computer system they spent thousands of dollars on. 

But, uh, what was the question? Sitting still? Yeah, I guess I'm usually bouncing my leg or messing with something on my desk.
Do these difficulties with restlessness, trouble focusing, or staying still interfere with your work, relationships, or daily life?

Well, I mean, it's not like I'm getting fired tomorrow or anything. I've been at the call center for, gosh, almost eight years now. But it is starting to show up in my performance reviews. My supervisor, Dave—he's a good guy, mostly, though he wears these really loud patterned ties that just clash with everything. I don't know where he buys them, probably one of those discount racks at the outlet mall. You know the ones, where everything is fifty percent off but it's all irregular sizes or weird colors. I went to the outlet mall a few months ago looking for a new pair of work shoes. I need something with good arch support because sitting all day actually wrecks your lower back if you aren't careful. I ended up getting these slip-on loafers, but they pinch a little on the right side. 

But anyway, Dave, he pointed out in my last review that I have a lot of unfinished tickets. And I guess I make some careless mistakes here and there, like forgetting to log a specific resolution code, which he says slows the whole team down. I really am trying hard, though. And I get along great with the customers! Most of them just want someone to actually listen to them instead of reading off a script. Like this one lady last week, she called in because her account was locked, and we ended up talking for twenty minutes about her grandson's little league team. They made it to the state semi-finals, which is pretty impressive for a town of only four thousand people. 

But yeah, the unfinished tickets and the mistakes... Dave says it's an issue. So I guess it does interfere a little bit at work.
Looking back, were you already having these kinds of difficulties with restlessness or staying focused before you turned 12 years old?

Before I was 12? Oh, yeah. I mean, this isn't just something that started when I moved to the call center or anything like that. It’s been around long before that. I remember back in grade school, my teachers were always writing the same things on my report cards. They'd say I was bright, but careless. And that I talked out of turn constantly. I always had to be reminded to just stay with my work and finish what I started. 

I actually found a box of those old report cards in my mom's attic when we were cleaning out her house last year. It’s a huge Victorian place, built in the late 1800s, I think. Beautiful woodwork, but the upkeep is just unbelievable. The draft from the windows in the winter is terrible. We had to put that plastic film over all of them, the kind you shrink with a hair dryer. Have you ever tried doing that? It's impossible to get it completely smooth. There's always one corner that wrinkles, and it drives me absolutely crazy. You have to hold the hair dryer at just the right angle, and even then, if the double-sided tape doesn't stick properly to the window frame... well, you're just heating up plastic for no reason. 

My mom kept everything, though. Every drawing, every report card, every little certificate. She had them all filed away in these old metal lockboxes. But yeah, reading through them, it was always the same story from the teachers. "Needs to focus," "Interrupts class," "Doesn't apply himself." So, yeah, I guess it’s always been like this.
